gaps.sentence: Listen! Someone ___ the violin in the flat above us.
gaps.hint: Listen signals an action happening now
gaps.explanation: 'Listen!' points to an action in progress at the moment of speaking, so the present continuous is used: is playing.

gaps.sentence: We ___ our cousins in Melbourne next month — the flights are booked.
gaps.hint: a booked arrangement for next month
gaps.explanation: A fixed personal arrangement takes the present continuous: are visiting.

gaps.sentence: I ___ getting up early because I have done it for years.
gaps.hint: be used to means present familiarity
gaps.explanation: 'Be used to' plus -ing means familiarity with something, here in the present: am used to.

gaps.sentence: This is the best pizza I ___ in years.
gaps.hint: superlative experience counted up to now
gaps.explanation: Superlative statements about experience up to now take the present perfect: have eaten.

gaps.sentence: When I came downstairs, the whole house ___ of fresh bread.
gaps.hint: smell as a state verb in past
gaps.explanation: 'Smell' as a state verb takes simple tenses, here the past simple: smelled.

gaps.sentence: Look at the time! We ___ discussing one agenda item for an hour.
gaps.explanation: 'For an hour' and still relevant — present perfect continuous.

gaps.sentence: By next April, we ___ here for ten years.
gaps.hint: duration leading up to a future point
gaps.explanation: A duration leading up to a future point takes the future perfect continuous: will have been living.

gaps.sentence: The company ___ its profits every year since it changed strategy, and analysts expect more growth.
gaps.hint: since clause anchors past to present
gaps.explanation: A 'since' clause connecting a past start to the present requires the present perfect: has increased.
